decisions.finding: The similarity score tops out at one, but no floor is given, so 0.72 for another category cannot be judged as close or far.
decisions.reason: Real. tickets.nearest_example: average_similarity_same_category 0.809, average_similarity_other_categories 0.716. The floor in this data is that second figure: tickets about other things still score about 0.72. A general 'two unrelated sentences score X' is not in facts.json and cannot be stated (SPEC rule 5).
decisions.change: Segment 3 narration: 'A gap, though not a wide one.' replaced by 'So the scale does not start near zero: tickets about other things still score high. Read the gap between scores, not the level.' Table note and the glossary entry for similarity score say the same.

decisions.finding: The brief says 'using an approved model' but the lesson never says what kinds of embedding model exist, what one costs, or who approves it.
decisions.reason: Hosted against in-house is a principle the lesson needs (and the 7-3 ruling depends on it). A price per thousand tickets is not in facts.json, and SPEC rule 5 forbids quoting outside figures, so the cost is made something the assistant must state before it sends anything. Who approves is organisation-specific; the lesson keeps the course's own rule from 1-5 (an approved destination).
decisions.change: Segment 8 item 1 now reads: 'Before anything is embedded, ask which model, what it will cost, and where the text goes. A hosted model receives every ticket. One that runs on your own machines does not. Client text needs an approved destination first.' The brief asks for hosted or in-house, the destination and the cost for [that many texts], then waits for a go-ahead. Audit item 1 and the 'embedding model' glossary entry (hosted or in-house; embedded once, stored and reused) follow.

decisions.finding: Two lessons of text work both run on support tickets; wants one run on ad headlines checked against policy.
decisions.reason: A new dataset and a re-based lesson. docs/council/DECISIONS.md already rejected 'Ad headlines instead of support tickets' (tickets give a clean labelled task; headlines appear in the questions).
decisions.change: None for the finding itself. The R1 sentence in segment 1 now names live ad headlines checked against policy as the same problem; quiz 3 and the transfer list already use headlines.

rulings.R1: Segment 1, one added sentence: 'That need is general: place any text by what it means, and you can find the live ad headlines repeating a claim policy already rejected, whatever their wording.'
rulings.R3: Brief rewritten as a template (115 words): slots for where the model may run, the text, the text column, the items to inspect, N neighbours, labelled examples per category, the baseline, and the easy/hard split. It now makes the assistant state model, hosting, destination and cost and wait before any text is sent.
rulings.R4: Recap is 48 spoken words, two sentences, cue markers removed, 'Keep this' card kept.
rulings.R5: Keyed answer is the longest option in 1 of 10. Replaced: the two 'Nothing ...' options in review 1 variant 1 (now a sentiment-score misreading and a label-everything-first misreading); 'Accept the 40' (quiz 1, now a margin-of-error misreading); 'Accept it' (review 2 variant 2, now 'run ten of your own'); the two 'Fine ...' options in quiz 4 (now two routing actions that keep the same misreadings); 'Agree:' in review 1 variant 3 (now 'Drop the 80:'). Whys extended. Keyed positions unchanged.
rulings.R6: Segment 8, one added sentence for the move that sat only in other_ways: 'When what you want has a fixed spelling, an error code or a product name, a plain keyword search is still the right tool.'
rulings.R7: Audit items reworded as things printed in the output: model, hosting, destination and quoted cost before any text is sent; neighbours with their scores; counts of training and test examples with none in both, beside the guessing baseline; accuracy by training size with the range, and the easy/hard split.
rulings.specific: Bag-of-words: the only bag-of-words figures in this lesson are the 'Word counts' series of the segment 6 chart, which already ends at 54.2 (tickets.learning_curve.rows[5].bag_of_words_accuracy 0.542, now equal to tickets.methods.bag_of_words_model.accuracy). All twelve points of the chart re-checked. 'It needs all 600 tickets to match what the embedding managed with twelve' is still true: 54.2 against 54.3. Test set of 450 is quoted once (review 2 variant 3) and is right. The ticket_map segment (4) is kept and its narration is byte-identical; checked against site/public/js/widgets.js and widgets.json: each dot is a ticket, 256 numbers drawn in 2, six categories in the legend, pointing at a category isolates it. Everything the narration says about the map is true.

open_questions: Cost (finding 1): facts.json holds no cost figure for embedding the tickets. If you want the lesson to say what it costs as a number, add it to tickets (for example cost of embedding 1,050 tickets) and segment 8 can quote it.
The map draws 360 of the 1,050 tickets (widgets.json ticket_map). The narration does not claim otherwise; add 'a sample of 360' to the widget note if you want it stated.
Narration is 930 words (SPEC aims at 900, hard cap 950) after the R1 and R6 sentences, the floor in segment 3 and the hosted/in-house lines in segment 8.
